title: TDD, AI agents and coding with Kent Beck
summary: Kent Beck describes coding with agents as an unpredictable genie, keeps fast tests to catch it, and recounts the history of XP, TDD and the Agile Manifesto.

assertions.quote: That's how I work all the time. So so so when you work with your genie, you start with the tests.

verdicts.note: Tests-first gives agents a target and limits test-cheating; evidence is mostly anecdotal and it does not suit all code (e.g. UI).

assertions.quote: I look at the code, and it's just a lookup table. It says if this is the input string, here's the output string

verdicts.note: Reward hacking on tests (special-casing, weakening or deleting tests) is documented by labs and in agent evaluations, though frequency varies by model and setup.

assertions.quote: those tests can be run all the time to catch the genie accidentally accidentally breaking things.

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.

assertions.quote: is not good at reducing coupling and increasing cohesion ... it has no taste, no sense of design.

verdicts.note: Linters and agent rules catch local smells, but architecture and coupling decisions still lack automated checks. Tooling is improving.

assertions.quote: 90% of my skills just went to zero dollars and 10% of my skills just went up a,000x.

verdicts.note: Plausible economic logic and widely argued, but not measured; execution, distribution and maintenance still matter.

assertions.quote: I'm programming in every language under the sun and I just I just kind of don't care. I'm learning by osmosis.

verdicts.note: AI clearly lowers the barrier to unfamiliar mainstream languages, but output quality still depends on the developer's ability to judge it and drops for less common languages.

assertions.quote: this is exactly like a slot machine. You got intermittent reinforcement. You got negative outcomes and positive outcomes.

verdicts.note: This describes subjective experience; no controlled data measures compulsive use of coding agents.

assertions.quote: organizations are going to have to get used to throwing away a lot more code because you can try ideas so much more cheaply.

verdicts.note: This is a strategic framing about how to organize product work rather than a measurable claim.
Anthropic: researchers run many Claude instances exploring different approaches, and the pre-training team uses Claude Code largely to run extra experiments; descriptive, with nothing on roadmaps.
